headers.//: Firebase defaults every file to max-age=3600, which is exactly wrong for the two kinds of file here. The catch-all makes the HTML revalidate; the rules after it override that for anything content-addressed. Order matters — later matches win.

Filenames carry a content hash, so a changed file is a different URL and this can never serve something stale. Without it a returning visitor kept the previous deploy's bundle for up to an hour — which is how the old build survived a deploy and loaded from cache in testing.
The Draco decoder is pinned to the three version in package.json and only changes when that does.

Font filenames encode family, subset, weight range and style, so a different font is a different file. These are the one asset a returning visitor should never re-fetch. Swapping a font means changing the filename, not just the bytes.
